item.title: Jaela Auguste shines, defense struggles in Wisconsin volleyball's win at Iowa
item.description: One of Wisconsin volleyball ’s streaks against its Big Ten neighbor to the southwest ended, but the more important streak stayed alive. The sixth-ranked Badgers defeated unranked Iowa in four sets, 25-16, 26-28, 25-21, 25-17, on Oct. 18 at Xtream Arena in Coralville, Iowa. The second set snapped the Badgers’ streak of 31 consecutive sets won against the Hawkeyes. UW did enough in the third and fourth sets, however, to win its 11th consecutive match against Iowa. Here are three takeaways from the win: Jaela Auguste has career day against Hawkeyes UW middle blocker Jaela Auguste showed why she was a 2025 third-team All-American with her performance against the Hawkeyes. Auguste finished with a career-high 20 kills while hitting .552. She also had at least a hand in five of UW’s seven blocks. The Florida transfer was a factor from start to finish. Her 12 combined kills in the first two sets were an early bright spot. She then punctuated the Badgers’ win with kills on each of their last three points in the match-clinching fourth set. Auguste was not the only middle blocker to shine against the Hawkeyes. Freshman Lynney Tarnow had 13 kills, coming up just short of her career-high of 16 kills in a five-set match against then-No. 17 Florida. Outside of the middle blocker position, Decelise Champion had 14 kills, six digs and two blocks. But the 17-year-old star also had seven attack errors – a season-high – and a .206 hitting percentage. Wisconsin ’s defense leads to subpar second set What Wisconsin did – or more so what it didn’t do – defensively played a large part in a rare set loss to the Hawkeyes. (The last one was more than eight years ago.) Iowa hit a match-high .405 in the second set and recorded more than twice as many kills than in the first set. It was a sharp contrast from Iowa’s .077 hitting percentage in the first set. It also stands out against an Iowa team that previously hit .162 against then-No. 16 Penn State, .211 against then-No. 22 Michigan State and .173 against No. 13 Purdue. While the defense might have been the biggest issue, there were other factors that put UW’s back row in a more difficult position. UW had only one block in the set and did not bring much serving pressure. Audrey Flanagan returns, Eva Travis takes first two sets off Wisconsin star freshman Audrey Flanagan returned to the starting lineup after sitting out against Maryland – a team with only two Big Ten wins so far. Sheffield said that it was simply a night off for Flanagan. Flanagan had nine kills while hitting .444 against Iowa. That was while Champion, Auguste and Tarnow took more swings than the freshman who has often shouldered heavy workloads. UW appeared to take a similar approach with usual starter Eva Travis sitting out the first and second sets. But after UW’s rare set loss to the Hawkeyes, Travis started the third set. Travis had three kills and one attack error in eight attempts. This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: Jaela A

item.title: Mike Vrabel’s Honest Patriots Take After Jets Win: ‘Lucky We Won’
item.description: Mike Vrabel’s Honest Patriots Take After Jets Win: ‘Lucky We Won’ originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Mike Vrabel did not try to dress up the Patriots ’ 26–19 win over the New York Jets. “Lucky we won, happy we won,” the New England coach said after Sunday’s game, according to Mike Reiss. It was a short assessment, but it captured the tension of an afternoon when the Patriots built a lead, let the Jets back into the game and needed one final play to protect the result. New England got the win and its third straight victory. Vrabel also made clear that the performance left plenty to review. A lead did not make the finish comfortable The Patriots went into halftime ahead 17–3 after Drake Maye threw touchdown passes to Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas. New York answered after the break, scoring 10 points in the third quarter and turning the fourth into a genuine test. Mike Vrabel: Lucky we won, happy we won. https://t.co/gOw6yKp506 — Mike Reiss (@MikeReiss) October 18, 2026 New England pushed its lead back to 10 when Maye found Hunter Henry for a touchdown, but the Jets kept coming. After a Jason Sanders field goal made it a one-score game, Andy Borregales’ 27-yard field goal gave the Patriots breathing room with 1:13 remaining. New York added another field goal, making the score 26–19, then tried an onside kick. Douglas recovered it. That play ended the Jets’ final chance and allowed the Patriots to close out a divisional win that had become much closer than the first-half score suggested. MORE : Patriots vs. Jets Score, Highlights: Patriots Hold On to Beat Jets Despite Multiple Injuries Vrabel knows the result does not erase the problems The Patriots also had to manage a difficult day up front, with multiple offensive linemen leaving because of injuries. New England lost a fumble during the Jets’ second-half push, giving its opponent another opportunity to make the comeback real. Those are the kinds of sequences that help explain Vrabel’s blunt reaction. The Patriots made enough plays to win, including the late field goal and Douglas’ recovery, but they also gave the Jets room to stay in it. That mix of relief and dissatisfaction is a useful snapshot of where New England stands. The Patriots have won three straight and improved to 4–2, yet Sunday was not the kind of clean performance that lets a team move on without corrections. Vrabel’s message was simple: enjoy the result, but recognize how close the game came to turning the other way. The schedule gives the Patriots little time to sit with it. They travel to face the Chicago Bears on Thursday night, making the quick turnaround an immediate test for a team coming off a physically demanding win. item.description: The Los Angeles Rams waived kicker Harrison Mevis after he missed a pair of field goals in the team’s Week 5 loss to the Buffalo Bills, signing Blake Grupe to replace him. item.title: Chelsea Are Among The Clubs Hoping To Land This Brighton Defender: Good Fit For Alonso?
item.description: Chelsea Are Among The Clubs Hoping To Land This Brighton Defender: Good Fit For Alonso? In a recent post on X , journalist Ekrem Konur stated that Chelsea are among the clubs hoping to land Brighton and Hove Albion defender Luka Vuskovic. It has been mentioned that the Blues are facing stiff competition from Bayern Munich, Barcelona and Real Madrid in the race to land the Croat talent next year. Vuskovic’s Decent Form In The Premier League This Season Vuskovic has enjoyed a good run of form at the English club in this campaign so far as he has managed to put in a run of solid performances for them in the Premier League. The Croat defender has been involved in ten matches for the Seagulls this season, scoring one goal and securing one assist in various competitions. The 19-year-old is currently one of the most gifted young centre-backs in the Premier League . Thus, it is no wonder that the Blues are eyeing a move for him next year. His current contract at the American Express Community Stadium will run out in the summer of 2031. Hence, Chelsea would have to launch a big offer if they are serious about recruiting Vuskovic this winter or at the end of this season. BRIGHTON, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 14: Luka Vuskovic of Brighton & Hove Albion looks on during the training session on day ahead of the UEFA Conference League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 at Brighton & Hove Albion Stadium on October 14, 2026 in Brighton, England. (Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty Images) Will Vuskovic Be A Good Fit For Chelsea Boss Xabi Alonso? Vuskovic loves a tackle and can scan the danger well to earn possession back for his side inside his half. He usually clears the danger when the opposition are on the offensive and can even use his strong 1.93m frame to win a few important aerial duels for his team. The Croat sensation is even proficient at playing his way out from the back. Vuskovic is getting used to the Premier League and won’t take much time to adjust to life at Chelsea if they can find a way to bring him on board next year. We can expect him to add more quality and depth to Chelsea head coach Xabi Alonso’s defence in the long run. Vuskovic will also help the Blues compete across all fronts over the next few years. At 19, the Croat whizkid has a bright future ahead of him. Hence, he would be an excellent fit for Chelsea’s needs in the long term. With all things considered, Alonso would be wise to acquire Vuskovic’s services next year.

item.title: Ella Toone ends WSL drought as Manchester United Women beat Charlton Athletic
item.description: Ella Toone ends WSL drought as Manchester United Women beat Charlton Athletic Manchester United Women made it three successive Women’s Super League victories with a commanding 3-1 win over Charlton Athletic at The Valley on Sunday afternoon. United unchanged at The Valley United manager Eva Olid selected the same starting XI that had beaten Liverpool 1-0 before the international break, keeping faith with an attacking unit featuring Jess Park, Toone , Medina and Elisabeth Terland. Ahead of the contest, it was relayed by The Peoples Person that Olid wanted every member of her squad ready for a demanding sequence of three games. First half United took control immediately and broke the deadlock in the sixth minute. Medina’s forward ball was not properly dealt with by Elisha N’Dow, allowing Toone to pounce and send an excellent looping effort in off the underside of the crossbar. The lead was doubled just four minutes later. Hanna Lundkvist surged forward from right-back and delivered across goal, where Medina arrived to guide a first-time finish into the bottom corner beyond Sophie Whitehouse. Charlton responded against the run of play in the 13th minute. Jodie Hutton supplied the cutback and Davidson finished past Phallon Tullis-Joyce to give the struggling hosts a route back into the contest. United did not allow that setback to disrupt their momentum. Hinata Miyazawa had an effort blocked before Zigiotti struck the crossbar as Olid’s team pushed to re-establish their two-goal advantage. The third goal eventually arrived after 31 minutes. Zigiotti started a slick move, exchanged passes with Park and stabbed the ball beyond Whitehouse to complete an eventful first half for the Swedish midfielder . Tullis-Joyce was required to make a smart save from Hutton before the interval, but United otherwise looked increasingly comfortable once they had regained their cushion. Second half Park drove forward and cut the ball back for Toone, although the midfielder placed her side-footed attempt wide of the post. Terland was next to threaten, turning her marker well before forcing Whitehouse into a good stop as United searched for a fourth goal. Olid used her bench with Wednesday’s Subway Players Cup fixture against Liverpool in mind. Simi Awujo replaced Zigiotti in the 69th minute, while Lea Schuller came on for Terland shortly afterwards. Schuller almost made an immediate impact when she beat Whitehouse after racing through on goal, only for her effort to rebound off the post. Fellow substitute Monica Jusu Bah also went close during stoppage time. There was no late route back for Charlton, who remain without a point after six league matches. Karen Hills’ side have scored only three times while conceding 18 goals during a difficult start to life back in the top flight. Momentum building under Olid The speed and precision of United’s opening spell were particularly encouraging given their occasional difficulty creating clear opportunities earlier in the campaign.

Skattebo — who still believes he is a No. 1 back — entered the game for the first time during that second Giants possession. He played a key role as a decoy on his first snap — a 20-yard end-around carry by Mooney that moved the Giants to their 43. Skattebo’s benching Sunday came a week after his overtime fumble cost the Giants a likely win in Washington. They were lucky to escape with a tie, after the Commanders botched the clock. It was Skattebo’s first lost fumble this season — but officially his fourth fumble overall. Harbaugh made it clear after the game that this could not continue. Harbaugh signed Harris, who is coming off a torn Achilles tendon, in mid-August. The move made sense, since Harbaugh wanted to — and still wants to — use a run-heavy approach on offense. But through the season’s first five games, Skattebo and Harris had both produced modest results, as both averaged just 3.6 yards per carry. Skattebo had carried 81 times, Harris 27. Tracy had worked his way back into a third-down role, after going through early season hiccups. Tracy entered entered Sunday with just seven carries this season — two fewer than Singletary, who had been a healthy scratch. Singletary on Sunday was active for a change. He hadn’t played since Week 2 in Los Angeles. As for ball security, Skattebo wasn’t the Giants’ only running back who had problems in that area early this season. (And in reality, he had three fumbles prior to Sunday — not four. Still, that’s less than ideal.) Tracy came into Sunday with one fumble this season (which he lost). Ditto for Harris — one fumble (which he lost). Yet ball security was only part of the Giants’ run-production issue. Coming out of Week 5, they ranked last in the NFL in a key rushing stat: Just 28% of their runs gained at least 2 yards before initial contact. That’s a run-blocking problem. The Giants’ offensive guard, Jon Runyan and rookie Francis Mauigoa, had been especially ineffective as run blockers during the first five games. Still, Sunday presented a chance for better results, since the Saints came into the game 29th in Pro Football Focus’ run defense ratings. The Giants, meanwhile, were 26th in rushing offense and 29th in run blocking. MORE GIANTS COVERAGE Giants’ rally falls short vs. Saints: Jameis Winston, Cam Skattebo benched. What’s next? item.title: Rams are in trouble after losing new kicker Blake Grupe to injury during Cardinals game
item.description: The Los Angeles Rams special teams unit has been a major talking point for a couple of years now. Head coach Sean McVay has frequently adjusted both the special teams coordinator and the kicker trying to get the unit to a stable place. Unfortunately it did not pan out through their first five games of the season, and it was on full display during Monday Night Football. In Week 5, Los Angeles had a chance to win the game against the Buffalo Bills, but kicker Harrison Mevis had his kick blocked and Buffalo went on to win in overtime instead. MORE: Rams make special teams changes following loss to Bills on MNF It marked the second missed kick of the game for Mevis, and a day later the Rams cut him. They turned to Blake Grupe, who they signed off the New York Jets practice squad to replace him. Sep 27, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay looks on during the first half against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) It started off well for Grupe during Sunday’s game against the Arizona Cardinals. The 27-year-old made his first field goal of the day, knocking one through the uprights from 44 yards out. However, the kickoff that followed would lead to an unfortunate turn. Grupe kicked it off and Cardinals returner Devin Duvernay broke a few tackles with Grupe as the last man he had to beat. Grupe pushed him out of bounds but injured himself in the process. Moments later, the Rams announced an update on his status , ruling him doubtful to return with a knee injury. Blake Grupe Goes Down in 1st Quarter Punter Ethan Evans is going to serve as the emergency kicker for now, but it is unlikely the Rams can rely on him for the rest of the game. For a special teams unit that has been a persistent problem for Los Angeles, losing their second kicker in less than a week is about as bad as it gets. McVay will have another difficult decision to make at the position before the Rams take the field again in Week 7 if Grupe’s injury sidelines him long-term. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

On the next play, Chuba Hubbard’s nice run was called back for a hold. On the next play, the Panthers were called for ineligible players down field, but that one was declined. Young found Tetairoa McMillan to pick up a first down either way. Dave Canales turtled from there and elected to let the clock run out. Neither team called any timeouts, and the game went into the half with the Panthers holding a 10-7 lead. Third Quarter The Panthers picked up a couple of first downs on the first drive. Devonta Smith briefly left the game after a hard fall, but he returned to catch a long touchdown over Will Lee. The Panthers bungled the kickoff and ended up deep in their own territory. The offense did nothing, then Sam Martin botched the punt. It looked like things were unraveling for Carolina, but the Eagles came to the rescue. A bad snap on first down put the Eagles way behind the sticks. The defense forced a punt, and Anthony Tyus broke through the line to block the punt. The offense finally took advantage of the field position. They picked up a first down with a Hubbard run, and an unnecessary roughness penalty tacked on more yardage. On the next play, Young found Tommy Tremble completely uncovered down the field for a touchdown. Tremble was called for taunting because he had the audacity to point in the general direction of an Eagles player. Ryan Fitzgerald missed the long extra point. The Panthers defense let the Eagles start moving the ball again, but Ejiro Evero dialed up the pressure when the Eagles got to midfield. Tre’von Moehrig notched a sack. On fourth down, McKee launched a jump ball to Smith, but Zaire Wheatley was able to range over and break up the pass. Chuba Hubbard grinded out a first down then David Moore took a bubble screen 27 yards inside the 15 yard line. One more first down run from Hubbard iced the game. Chuba Hubbard had an admirable workhorse performance with 28 carries for 120 yards, and Bryce Young put together a quiet 281 yards passing, even if the completion percentage wasn’t great. On defense, Will Lee IV did a very good job on DeVonta Smith, who was basically the only offensive weapon the Eagles had left. The group did what they should have done against an opponent with a makeshift offensive line and dearth of play makers. They limited the Eagles to just 3.6 yards per play. The penalties are really the only thing that kept the Eagles in the game. The Panthers move to 3-2 with the win. It’s their first winning record since they started the 2021 season 3-0. They’ll try to keep that momentum going when they host the division rival Buccaneers next Sunday.

item.description: It was yet another record day for Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith in Week 7. Smith set a new Big Ten record with his 39th career receiving touchdown in Ohio State's big road win at Indiana. HE broke a tie with Michigan's Braelon Edwards after tying the record a week ago. Smith will continue to add to his record total as Ohio State is only halfway through the regular season, and expected to play a handful of postseason games. Already with 12 receiving touchdowns, nobody looks to be catching Smith this season in the Big Ten. Nobody else in the conference has hit double digits, although KJ Duff of Rutgers and Colin Dixon are each one away. Penn State's Chase Sowell has moved up into the top 10 of the Big Ten receiving yardage leaders after a big game in a losing effort against Michigan. Penn State is still missing Koby Howard, who got off to an electric start this season, but Chase Sowell has been stepping up in recent weeks to provide a reliable passing option for Rocco Becht. item.title: Lautaro Martinez’s injury lay-off is matter of concern for Inter in the long and short terms
item.description: Lautaro Martinez’s injury lay-off is matter of concern for Inter in the long and short terms Inter’s midweek blues got worse after their defeat at home to Club Brugge in the Champions League, with Lautaro Martínez now set for weeks on the sidelines after scoring a brace against the Belgian giants. While they did manage to go past Bologna, there is a chance the Argentine will be missed. The Nerazzurri captain picked up a strain in his left hanstring, which medical tests revealed the following day. While the club haven’t provided an exact return date, La Gazzetta dello Sport are expecting the 29-year-old to sit out through next month’s international break, with Inter’s trip to Atalanta later in the month being considered his next potential outing. This is a tough fixture run-in for Inter to brace without their captain and star striker, as they have Champions League fixtures against Shakhtar and Feyenoord during this period, as well as key league matches against Milan and Como, putting massive pressure on their grip at the top of the Serie A summit. In the here and now, unless there are more injuries, Inter should be able to pull through. Pio Esposito and Marcus Thuram have already featured together upfront, with the former in particular attracting attention through his performances for both Inter and Italy early in the season. Thuram will take over the role of senior forward in Lautaro’s absence, while Ange-Yoan Bonny is another option; the Ivorian hasn’t set the world alight since move from Parma last summer, but now he could get more minutes. It’s not the short-term need for a fix, though. A hamstring strain for a player late in his 20s strongly indicate that minutes are catching up with Martínez, who has been a regular in Inter’s line-up pretty much since his arrival from Racing Club over eight summers ago. Between the 2018/19 and 2025/26 seasons, the 2022 World Cup winner missed 207 days (35 games) through injury, though he missed 13 games last season alone, hinting that his lay-offs may become more frequent. This leave Inter in a precarious position. They need to reduce their reliance on Lautaro in the long term, and it doesn’t look like relying on Esposito, Thuram, and Bonny alone will suffice. If things don’t improve in terms of output from these three as well as Lautaro’s availability, Inter may find themselves in the transfer market looking for a new striker as early as January. Anshuman Joshi | GIFN

item.title: Another unremarkable win shows Arsenal’s strength is in depth rather than creativity | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Champions so risk-averse Forest were lured into thinking they had a chance, until bench was used to see them off Pass. Pass. Pass. Pass. Sideways. Square. Backwards. Pass. Pass. Recycle. Pass. It wasn’t much of a spectacle. But in the end, for the second week running, thanks in no small part of their bench, Arsenal won. Fireworks in the autumn are for Bonfire Night; titles require relentless accumulation. Since the international break, Arsenal have won three games out of three despite not being in the lead at half-time in any of them. Hammered at Brighton and having endured a drab first hour at home to Leeds last week, there has been a rare sense, for the first time really since Manchester City dropped points at Everton at the beginning of May, of Arsenal not being quite at their best, needing to reassert their quality. This was not a performance that would terrify any opponent, but it did highlight Arsenal’s consistency and it did demonstrate just how deep their squad now runs. Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? item.description: Manchester City unrepentant in victory, Spurs make progress of a sort and Noni Madueke meets the moment The manner of Manchester City’s victory at Liverpool was an article of both vindication and vilification. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: Mikel Arteta’s new contract reflects where the power now lies at Arsenal | Ed Aarons
item.description: From transfers to stadium works and even the training-ground dog, there is no doubting the Spaniard’s influence at the club If anyone doubts Mikel Arteta’s status as No 1 at Arsenal in the week he committed his future to the club until 2030 , just ask Win the dog. The chocolate labrador who played a starring role in the celebrations when Arsenal were crowned Premier League champions in May has become part of the family at the training ground in Hertfordshire since being introduced by Arteta in May 2023. Kai Havertz, David Raya and Mikel Merino, who issues commands in Spanish and has spoken about spending time with Win when out for three months with a foot injury, are particular favourites. But, according to sources close to Win, a therapy dog trained not to bark, there is no contest when it comes to her preferred human: Arteta. Continue reading...

item.title: Lionel Messi’s Argentina career turned football into a sacred mystery
item.description: Jorge Messi wanted his country to fall in love with his son. That ambition was fulfilled during a brilliant international career that ended this week “What Argentina is doing in this World Cup is of a sacred order,” Brazilian writer Milly Lacombe posted at the height of the tide of anti-Argentinian sentiment during this year’s tournament. She was exploring the contradiction she felt around her support of Lionel Messi: “a player who is a God and a man who shakes Trump’s hand”. Lacombe highlighted the importance of acknowledging the complexities around Messi and the Argentinian team. How is it possible that Messi was not speaking out against the racist incidents we all saw around the Argentina team , she asked. “That’s why it hurts so much to see someone with Messi’s power choosing to make himself small,” she wrote. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
